name: SparkToro
description: Audience research from Rand Fishkin (Moz's co-founder): describe your audience in a sentence and get the podcasts, YouTube channels, subreddits, newsletters, and keywords they actually follow - plus the AI prompts they type. The tool for finding cheap attention before you spend a dollar.
pricing_details: Free $0/mo: 3 audience previews per month, single user, preview data only. Personal is annual-only: $450/year shown as $38/mo, with 4 full reports per month, one user, all data types, custom logo on reports, and MCP access. Business costs $112/mo billed annually ($1,344/yr) or $150/mo monthly: 25 reports/month, 10 users, Take Action advice, and Persona Builder. Agency is $225/mo billed annually ($2,700/yr) or $300/mo monthly: 250 reports/month, 100 users, SSO, SCIM provisioning, and payment by ACH or wire. A separate public API is sold as pay-as-you-go credit bundles outside the subscription. Every paid report includes the same data types: demographics, social accounts and networks, websites, press and publications, podcasts, YouTube channels, subreddits, apps and AI tools, search keywords, bio keywords, and the AI prompts the audience uses. The MCP server connects SparkToro to ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor free on paid plans. Cancellation is online and anytime, but partial-period refunds are not offered - the annual Personal plan commits the whole $450.
platform: Web app + browser extension + MCP server (paid plans) + REST API (separate product)
pros: Answers the question every other tool skips: where does my audience already pay attention - podcasts, subreddits, YouTube, newsletters, ranked by affinity
Free plan with 3 previews a month lets you sanity-check whether SparkToro knows your niche before paying anything
AI prompt data (2026) shows what your audience actually asks ChatGPT-class tools - an early-mover signal for AI-search visibility work

Report data doubles as outreach lists: sponsorship targets, guest-podcast pitches, and PR contacts with contact info on Business
cons: Metered reports punish occasional users: 4 reports/month on Personal drew a genuine G2 complaint - '$40 a month just for 4 reports... overpriced'

features: Audience search from a plain sentence - 'vegan home cooks who follow plant-based nutrition creators' style queries
Affinity-ranked lists of podcasts, YouTube channels, subreddits, websites, and press your audience consumes

faq.question: What is the difference between a preview and a report?
faq.answer: The free plan gives 3 previews a month with sampled, preview-only data - enough to judge whether SparkToro's panel covers your niche, not enough to plan a campaign. Paid plans return full reports: complete affinity rankings, demographics, keywords, and AI prompt data. A practical pattern from long-time users: run your two or three core audience searches on free previews first, then buy Personal only if the data looks alive.

faq.question: Why is Personal annual-only, and can I just buy one month?
faq.answer: SparkToro sells Personal only as a $450/year commitment shown as $38/mo. The first plan billable month-to-month is Business at $150/mo - a known friction point for solo researchers. The workaround experienced users adopt: buy one month of Business ($150), run a burst of 25 reports across all client projects, then cancel - 25 monthly reports at $6 each beats 4 annual reports at $9.38 each unless you research every single month.

faq.question: How accurate is the data?
faq.answer: SparkToro builds reports from large-scale clickstream and social-profile panels - estimates of where an audience spends attention, not survey responses. For audiences in the tens of thousands and up, the affinity rankings are consistently useful for picking sponsorships and outreach targets. For tiny, hyper-niche audiences the numbers get noisy; treat rankings as directional and cross-check a top podcast or subreddit by hand before spending money on it.

content:
## What SparkToro Actually Is

SparkToro answers the question every keyword tool ignores: before your audience ever searches, where do they already hang out? Describe the people you want in one sentence - the site's own example is "vegan home cooks who follow plant-based nutrition creators" - and a report returns affinity-ranked lists of the podcasts they download, the YouTube channels they watch, the subreddits where they ask real questions, the newsletters and sites they read, the accounts they follow, plus demographics, search keywords, bio keywords, and since 2026 the AI prompts they type into assistants.

It was built by Rand Fishkin, who co-founded Moz and then spent years arguing that modern marketing spends too much on renting search traffic and too little on owning attention. The tool operationalizes that argument with clickstream and social-panel data. In 2026 it also grew an MCP server on paid plans, so you can pull audience data inside ChatGPT or Claude, and AI prompt data that shows what your audience actually asks AI tools - an early signal for anyone doing AI-search visibility work.

What it is not: a rank tracker, a backlink checker, or a site auditor. It sits next to your SEO tools, not inside them.

## The Money Angle

1. **Buy attention where it's cheap.** The classic play: find three podcasts or two newsletters your niche listens to that nobody else is sponsoring, and buy slots before they get discovered. A $300 podcast ad in front of 5,000 exactly-right listeners routinely outperforms $1,500 of cold Google Ads - and SparkToro is how you find those slots.

2. **Guest spots instead of ads.** Every paid report lists the podcasts, YouTube channels, and publications your audience trusts, ranked. Work the list as a pitching target: guest appearances convert better than ads and cost only your time.

3. **Sell audience research as a service.** Freelance marketers run client audits through SparkToro - "here is where your buyers actually spend attention, here is your 90-day plan" - at $500-1,500 per engagement. One monthly Business plan (25 reports) covers many clients.

4. **AEO before your competitors.** The AI prompt data shows the questions your audience asks ChatGPT and Perplexity. Write pages that answer those prompts and you're early to a ranking surface most niches still ignore.

5. **Positioning language.** Bio keywords show how your audience describes itself. Copy their words into headlines and ad copy and watch relevance climb - it is message-market fit with a data source.

## What It Really Costs

| Plan | Monthly billing | Annual billing | Reports/mo | Users | Notable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | $0 | 3 previews | 1 | Preview data only |
| Personal | — | $450/yr ($38/mo) | 4 | 1 | All data types, MCP, annual-only |
| Business | $150/mo | $112/mo ($1,344/yr) | 25 | 10 | Take Action, Persona Builder |
| Agency | $300/mo | $225/mo ($2,700/yr) | 250 | 100 | SSO, SCIM, API/ACH |

Cost-per-report math decides the plan: Personal works out near $9.38 per report, Business annual near $4.48. The AI-facing API is a separate pay-as-you-go product. No partial refunds on any plan - cancel and access runs to the period's end.

## The Honest Cons

- **The meter is the product's biggest flaw.** Four reports a month on Personal is thin for active researchers, and G2 reviewers have said so in exactly those words. Burst users should buy Business monthly, binge, and cancel.
- **Annual lock-in without refunds.** $450 committed, no partial refunds. The free previews exist precisely so you test before that decision.
- **Panel estimates, not ground truth.** Clickstream plus social panels; small niches wobble. Directionally strong, precisely weak.
- **It complements SEO tooling rather than replacing it** - no ranks, no links, no audits, and no keyword volume database in the Ahrefs sense.
- **Monthly flexibility starts at $150.** Solo users who want one cheap flexible month are boxed into the annual choice.

## vs The Field

| | SparkToro | GummySearch | Brandwatch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core data | Multi-platform affinity (podcasts, YouTube, Reddit, sites, AI prompts) | Reddit-only audience mining | Enterprise social listening |
| Entry price | Free / $450-yr | ~$29-79/mo | Sales-call pricing, enterprise $$ |
| AI prompt data | Yes (2026) | No | Partial |
| Sponsorship/outreach lists | Core feature | Weak | Partial |
| Best for | Solo marketers and small agencies buying attention | Reddit-first content idea mining | Big-brand social teams |

Against the pages already on this site: GummySearch digs deeper inside Reddit specifically and costs less; SparkToro is the multi-platform upgrade once your monetization plan includes podcasts, YouTube, PR, or AI-search positioning. Brandwatch serves a different budget entirely.

## Bottom Line

SparkToro is the research tool for the make-money-with-AI crowd that is tired of guessing where to appear. Its reports convert directly into sponsorship buys, guest pitches, and AI-prompt content targets - attention moves, not vanity metrics. The metering and the annual-only Personal plan are genuine annoyances, so the working pattern is: three free previews to validate your niche, one monthly Business binge at $150 for a campaign burst, and a yearly commitment only once research becomes a weekly habit. The data is estimation, not gospel - but it is the only affordable tool that answers "where do these people already pay attention" instead of "what do they type into Google."
